content.text:
Fixed in `target-app/src/App.tsx`. Three changes:

- **`readStoredTheme()`** (`App.tsx:12`) — reads `kane-notes-theme` from `localStorage`, wrapped in try/catch so private mode or blocked storage falls back to light instead of throwing during render.
- **`useState(readStoredTheme)`** (`App.tsx:31`) — passed as a lazy initializer, so storage is read once on mount rather than on every render.
- **The existing theme effect** (`App.tsx:41`) now writes the value back alongside setting `document.body.dataset.theme`, so every toggle persists.

Verified: Kane's browser run against the live app reports green on `tests/darkmode_test.md`, including the "Verify dark mode survived" step after a fresh navigation, and `npm run typecheck` passes clean.

One thing worth flagging that the test doesn't cover: on a dark-mode reload there's a brief light flash, because React only applies the theme after the first paint. Eliminating it needs an inline script in `index.html` that sets `document.body.dataset.theme` before the bundle loads — outside the `./src`-only rule I was working under, so I left it. Say the word and I'll add it.
